newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to extend Golan Heights peacekeeping.
newsitem.headline: Japan to extend Golan Heights peacekeeping.

text.p: Japan said on Tuesday it would extend the term of duty of its military unit taking part in U.N. peacekeeping operations in the Golan Heights for an additional two years beyond next February.

"In light of strong requests from the United Nations and countries concerned, we have decided to extend the term for two more years from next February," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a regular news conference.
"Japan's activity has been highly praised by U.N. officials including the Secretary-General (Kofi Annan) and countries such as Syria and Israel," he said.
Japan's 45-member army logistics unit is part of the 1,000-member U.N. Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) which also comprises troops from Poland, Austria and Canada.

The unit from the Japan's Ground Self-Defence Force, or army, was sent to the Golan Heights in February 1996 for a two-year term, Tokyo's first contribution to a peacekeeping operation in the Middle East.
Japan has also sent troops for U.N. peacekeeping operations in Cambodia and Mozambique and to Zaire in support of a relief operation for Rwandan refugees.
